title: The Sixty-Week Spine
budget: INR 0 - free tiers only, serverless (no VPS)

phases.name: The shipping ritual
phases.theme: Build the machine that builds the projects. You will repeat this ritual ~20 times; every hour spent here is repaid five times.
phases.exit: You can go from `mkdir` to a live URL with tests, CI, a signed image and a working README in under 40 minutes without looking anything up.
verify_topics: Node.js LTS line and EOL dates

projects.pitch: A TypeScript project template that goes from clone to live URL in ten minutes, with tests, CI and supply-chain checks already wired.
Point it at a package.json and it tells you how far behind you are - latest version, release date, and how long since the project last shipped anything.

phases.name: SQL and the wire
phases.theme: The two things AI is worst at faking for you: a schema that survives contact with real data, and knowing what actually happens between a browser and your server.
phases.exit: You can design a normalized schema, write a window-function query, read an EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) plan and name the index that fixes it, and describe a TLS 1.3 handshake and an SSE stream - all from memory.

projects.pitch: Twelve analytical questions against a real public dataset, answered in SQL, with every query's plan and the index that made it fast.
The CLI grows a memory: scans, packages, versions and findings persisted in a schema that can answer 'what changed since last week?'
Paste a URL, get the full story: DNS chain, TLS handshake, certificate chain, negotiated HTTP version, every header, and what your caching setup is actually doing.
The same live counter built three ways - polling, SSE, WebSocket - with the bytes and latency to show when each one is the right answer.

phases.name: TypeScript and API design
phases.theme: Types that do work, and REST that someone can integrate against without messaging you.
phases.exit: You can type an API boundary end-to-end with zero `any`, and design a paginated, idempotent, versioned, rate-limited endpoint with an OpenAPI contract without reference.

projects.pitch: A client and server that cannot disagree, and eight bugs the type system refuses to compile.
A REST API you could hand to a stranger: cursor pagination, idempotent writes, machine-readable errors, and an OpenAPI contract.
Eight queries, written twice - raw SQL and Drizzle - with the SQL each one actually emits and what the planner does with it.
The driftwatch test suite: unit tests that run in 2 seconds and integration tests that run against a real Postgres in CI.

phases.name: Auth and the security baseline
phases.theme: The one area where a wrong AI-generated snippet costs you the job rather than a review comment.
phases.exit: You can implement password + session auth, a complete OAuth 2.1 + PKCE flow, and a passkey ceremony from scratch - and given any bug, name its OWASP Top 10 category.

projects.pitch: Three ways to keep a user logged in, one of them deliberately broken, and a page that shows you exactly how it breaks.
A working OAuth 2.1 authorization server and client, built from the spec rather than from a library.
Passkey registration and authentication, ceremony by ceremony, with the fallback flow nobody builds.
Multi-tenant driftwatch with passkeys, API keys and roles - plus a written threat model that names its own weaknesses.

phases.name: Ship it like you'll be paged
phases.theme: The phase that converts 'works on my machine' into a hiring signal. Docker, a supply-chain-aware pipeline, and the three signals.
phases.exit: You can containerize a Node service into a <150 MB multi-stage image, wire a pipeline that tests, scans, signs and deploys, and answer 'what happened at 3am?' from traces and logs rather than guesswork.
verify_topics: GitHub Actions pricing and free minutes

projects.pitch: One Node service, five Dockerfiles, and the numbers that show which choices actually matter.
A reusable GitHub Actions workflow that tests, scans, generates an SBOM, signs the artifact, and deploys - that other repos can call in three lines.
One trace that follows a scan from the API edge, through Postgres, out to the npm registry, and back.
SLOs as code for driftwatch, burn-rate alerts that fire, a public dashboard, and a postmortem for an outage you caused on purpose.

phases.name: Production backend
phases.theme: Caching, work off the request path, realtime at scale, and knowing your own numbers.
phases.exit: You can pick a cache strategy and defend it against two alternatives, run background work idempotently, and produce a load-test graph showing where your service falls over and why.

projects.pitch: The same endpoint at four cache layers, with the hit rates and latencies that tell you which one was worth it.
Scanning moves off the request path - with a duplicate delivery you can prove you survive.
Live presence for many people in one room, on Durable Objects, with an honest answer about what happens when the connection drops.
Load-test driftwatch until it breaks, find out why, fix it, and show the graph.

phases.name: The AI backend layer
phases.theme: The fastest-growing backend niche - and the phase where 'I built a wrapper' and 'I built an eval pipeline' are two different salary bands.
phases.exit: You can ship an LLM feature with streaming, a cost budget, a golden-dataset eval running in CI, and an honest published write-up of what your retrieval gets wrong.
verify_topics: Claude Agent SDK / OpenAI Agents SDK / Google ADK
frontier + open-weight model lineup and per-token pricing
free LLM API tiers (Gemini, Groq, Workers AI, GitHub Models)

projects.pitch: A provider-agnostic LLM gateway that streams, fails over, meters every token, and refuses to bankrupt you.
Prompts as versioned, tested files - with an injection suite that fails the build.
A golden dataset, an LLM judge, and a CI job that tells you whether your last prompt change made things worse.
Ask 'what actually breaks if I go from React Router 7 to 8?' and get a cited answer built from the real release notes.
An MCP server on the current spec that lets Claude Code ask your service what's rotting in a repo.
An agent that reads your changelog RAG, decides an upgrade is safe, opens a real PR, and waits for a human to say yes.
Measured cost reduction on driftwatch's LLM spend, with the before-and-after numbers.

phases.name: Distributed systems and interview reps
phases.theme: The vocabulary of the system design round, learned by building the smallest honest version of each idea.
phases.exit: You can whiteboard a rate limiter, a feed and a chat system with numbers attached, and explain in one sentence why exactly-once delivery is a lie.

projects.pitch: A database write and a Kafka event that cannot diverge, plus a duplicate delivery you survive on purpose.
Two services, one .proto contract, a streaming method, generated stubs in the repo, and a load test.
Three nodes, one leader, and a network partition that doesn't produce two of them.
driftwatch packaged for Kubernetes at the workload level - the layer you'd actually be asked about.
Twelve system design write-ups with real numbers, real diagrams, and a 'what I'd cut' section on each.

phases.name: Capstone and launch
phases.theme: The spine becomes a product with real users, and you start applying.
phases.exit: driftwatch v1.0 is live with a public dataset, all 22 READMEs pass the 60-second test, and 20+ applications are out.
verify_topics: every tool in the driftwatch stack
all free-tier limits you depend on
hiring-market signals (senior/junior posting mix, AI-role growth)

projects.pitch: Know what rotted in your dependency tree while you weren't looking - with the changelog evidence for every claim.
